findings.problem: Deployed legacy admin_update_all_profiles permits owners to update their own role and billing fields; permissive policies OR together, bypassing the stricter policy. API key update policies also bypass immutable-field checks, and api_usage permits public INSERT.
findings.status: Applied to the shared backend; all 24 PostgreSQL checks and real customer-token profile/key/usage boundaries passed.
findings.evidence: Twenty-four PostgreSQL tests plus remote history, trigger and grants inspection. Anonymous usage insertion returned HTTP 401 and PostgreSQL 42501 after deployment.

findings.problem: Six deployed edge functions reject the existing preview origin via CORS by returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://www.aidotnet.dev to requests from https://test.aidotnet.dev.
findings.status: Deployed minimal CORS wrapper to six existing handlers; preflight verified and community registration passed against preview
findings.evidence: Read-only OPTIONS checks against billing-portal, delete-account, register-community-license, issue-license, admin-resend-license-email, and validate-license. Regression tests cover preflight and actual error responses, production and preview origins, rejected lookalikes, and concurrent request isolation.

findings.remaining: Template sampling remains explicit. Phone crawls now re-exercise shared controls with a real mobile device context. Real business outcomes are asserted separately.

Backend webhook contracts use external boundary doubles; the separate hosted delayed-payment journey verifies actual signature checking, database writes and current Stripe subscription handling with signed injected events.
Existing new-customer journey injects a signed checkout event instead of completing a payment.

A passing test count is not a claim that every possible user state or path was exercised.

adversarial_review.issue: Normalized dot segments could turn a same-origin redirect into a protocol-relative navigation.
adversarial_review.resolution: Reject normalized // pathnames; unit and callback/login regressions cover the escape.

adversarial_review.issue: A scheduled cancellation later than renewal blocked the cancel-then-delete path.
adversarial_review.resolution: Authenticated cancel_before_renewal action selects the customer-owned subscription and changes the end without proration; confirm/dismiss/retry and real trial journey added.

adversarial_review.issue: Delayed success, invoice or update events could replay stale subscription state.
adversarial_review.resolution: Reconcile current Stripe status and price tier; preserve canceled and revoked licenses; retry provider/database failures.

adversarial_review.issue: Permissive legacy RLS policies bypassed protected-field policies.
adversarial_review.resolution: Applied reviewed trigger-backed policies, clamped repaired-profile identity/audit fields, denied key reactivation, revoked untrusted usage INSERT and preserved restrictive policies.

adversarial_review.issue: Database regression setup did not reproduce the deployed public usage policy.
adversarial_review.resolution: Prove anon and customer insertion succeeds with the legacy policy before migration and fails afterward; verify atomic migration/history rollback.

adversarial_review.issue: Crawler could miss errors, skip reachable duplicate controls or reject valid streamed-response controls.
adversarial_review.resolution: Record application console failures synchronously, await response bodies, track attempts by selector, anchor CSS paths and include visible pointer-disabled controls.

adversarial_review.issue: Auth configuration and manual preview verification could race the build/alias update.
adversarial_review.resolution: Auth prerequisite is explicit; build, backend release and manual preview runs share a lock without reusable-workflow deadlock.

adversarial_review.issue: Keyboard coverage alternated between only two dialog controls.
adversarial_review.resolution: Traverse every enabled stop consecutively in both directions and assert full wrap/containment.

adversarial_review.issue: Code deployment required unavailable secret-management permissions and could overwrite a separately rotated key.
adversarial_review.resolution: Preserve installed credentials during source deployment; leave explicit digest-verified rotation script for appropriately scoped operators and verify mail through actual hosted journeys.

adversarial_review.issue: PostgreSQL fixture readiness could connect during temporary initialization.
adversarial_review.resolution: Wait for final TCP readiness; 24 local and CI database checks passed.

adversarial_review.issue: The report had ambiguous deployed and production-write scope.
adversarial_review.resolution: Record preview frontend, shared production backend writes, migration/function deployment and external configuration separately.

adversarial_review.issue: Anonymous signup exploration left test users after otherwise successful crawls.
adversarial_review.resolution: Track only newly generated form emails, delete matching signup fixtures in finally across both contexts, preserve pre-existing addresses, and verify cleanup with the affected hosted anonymous crawl.

verification_boundaries: Stripe event destination settings were updated and confirmed by the owner; the restricted repository key cannot independently inspect them.
Payment verification uses disposable card-free trials and signed injected events, not a settled payment.
OAuth checks cover provider handoff; mail acceptance and generated links do not prove external consent or mailbox receipt.
Templated pages are sampled in browser contexts and all generated routes are checked by HTTP. Passing results do not claim every possible external-provider state.
